detail: Seizures recorded between 2015 and 2021 involved around 4,000 animal and plant species, about 3,250 of them listed by CITES. Some 140,000 seizures were reported by 162 countries and territories.

fact: Rhino, pangolin and elephant make up 72% of animal seizures
detail: Of animal seizures from 2015 to 2021, rhinoceros accounted for 29%, pangolins 28% and elephants 15%. Among plants, cedars and other Sapindales were 47%, rosewoods 35%, and agarwood and other Myrtales 13%.

fact: It is not only animals: timber is a third of plant seizures
detail: Rosewoods alone were 35% of plant seizures between 2015 and 2021. CITES protects more plants than animals: of the roughly 41,000 species listed, about 34,000 are plants.

fact: One in five land vertebrates is traded
detail: About 18% of terrestrial vertebrate species, nearly 5,600 in all, are traded internationally, 40 to 60% more than earlier estimates. A further 3,196 related species may be drawn in as the trade expands.

fact: The pangolin is the most trafficked wild mammal
detail: Close to a million pangolins are estimated to have been trafficked between 2000 and 2019. In Asia alone, more than 330 tonnes of pangolins and their parts were seized between 2015 and 2021.

fact: South Africa lost 352 rhinos to poaching in 2025
detail: Down from 420 in 2024, a 16% fall. 266 were killed on state land and 86 on private reserves, with 175 in Kruger National Park alone.

source.name: South Africa, Dept. of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment

fact: About 100 tonnes of baby eels are smuggled out of Europe each year
detail: Europol estimates roughly 100 tonnes of glass eels leave the EU illegally every season for Asian farms, where a kilogram can fetch over €5,000. One 2024–25 operation seized 22 tonnes across 21 countries.
Roughly 6,700 animal and 34,300 plant species are listed across the three CITES appendices, which set what may be traded across borders, and on what terms.

fact: Two decades of effort have not ended it
detail: UNODC's 2024 review found no clear downward trend in the overall scale of trafficking, even where enforcement cut specific flows, such as ivory and rhino horn.

fact: Parrots & songbirds appears in more WildTrace cases than any other group
detail: 137 of 1,331 cases name it, from 59 countries in all.
caveat: Counted in WildTrace's own cases, which come from the newsrooms and government sites searched, in the languages searched. It shows where wildlife crime is reported, not where it happens.
